newsitem.title: GUINEA: Mob burns opposition headquarters in Guinea.
newsitem.headline: Mob burns opposition headquarters in Guinea.

text.p: A mob ransacked and set fire to the headquarters of Guinea's main opposition party, the Guinean People's Rally, shortly after the return of its leader Alpha Conde from a European tour, party officials said on Sunday.

The Saturday night incident, blamed by party officials on political rivals, took place after clashes on Conde's route home from the airport between his supporters and students from a secondary school complex in the capital's Matam district.
Party supporters accused the students of hurling stones at the opposition welcoming procession.
A local official of the ruling Party of Unity and Progress rejected suggestions that its militants were involved.
President Lansana Conte, an army general who seized power in 1984, defeated Conde in a widely disputed 1993 presidential election as part of a sometimes bloody democratic transition.
In February, he weathered a bloody army pay revolt, which he described at the time as a veiled coup attempt.
The next presidential election is scheduled for 1998.
